note: Cases CLAUDE.md invariant 7 and registry-oracle-notes.md §11 name as the known ways to be confidently wrong. Each defeated some plausible parser.

cases.label: raw KeyedCodec + true THIRD ARGUMENT = required
cases.why: `new KeyedCodec("Shapes", new MapCodec<...>(...), true)` - raw, so a pattern expecting KeyedCodec<T> skips it and undercounts; and required by the third argument, so stopping at the first balanced paren keeps the key but loses its requiredness. Its four keys include exactly one required.

cases.label: raw KeyedCodec + true INSIDE the inner constructor = NOT required
cases.why: Same key NAME `Shapes`, also raw, but `new KeyedCodec("Shapes", new SetCodec<...>(..., true))` - two arguments, the true inside the inner constructor. Attributing it to the outer codec manufactures a requirement, and invariant 7 calls that the dangerous direction: a fabricated *required* can never be contradicted by a shipped asset.

cases.label: requiredness by Validators.nonNull() attached AFTER append(...) closes
cases.why: CLAUDE.md: `Name` is the sole key carrying Validators.nonNull(). Parsing to the first balanced paren reports NO required keys at all, because the validator attaches on the builder two calls further along, before .add().

cases.label: same simple name, different file, different key and requiredness
cases.why: The twin of the `StartObjective` interaction in the 44. Both declare exactly ONE key, so a count cross-check agrees while the key name and its requiredness are both wrong: this one is `ObjectiveId`, not required; the registered interaction is `Setup`, required.
